description: [The Conversation Africa] The super El Niño developing in the Pacific is expected to strengthen towards the end of 2026 and persist into early 2027. It's set to intensify dangerous heat and cause severe drought across parts of Africa. This is likely to mean more heat-related illness and deaths, worsening water shortages and greater disruption to electricity, food supplies and essential services.
